Filter and Refine

Finding a face's nearest neighbor among 337 faces takes 336 distances of 3,000 pixels each. Filter-and-refine first compares only K PCA numbers per face, keeps the K' closest candidates, and computes full distances for those alone. Find out how often that misses the true nearest face, and how a simple stopping rule makes the search exact.

The bars never cross the ticks
Every blue bar ends at or below its black tick: the distance in PCA numbers is never larger than the full distance, because projecting onto a few perpendicular directions can only shorten a vector. That one fact is what makes the exact version possible.

    
The stop rule
Walk down the list in PCA order, computing full distances. Once the next blue bar is longer than the best black tick found so far, stop: every face further down is at least that far away in full. The answer is guaranteed to be the true nearest face.

    
Approximate is often good enough
With a fixed K' the search is approximate: if the true nearest face is not among the candidates, it is never examined. Web-scale image search accepts that trade, with far more elaborate indexes, because an almost-nearest neighbor found in milliseconds beats the exact one found in minutes.
